thread:
The Audit Trail: Why Having Logs Isn't Enough for Compliance

Quick thread 🧵

> An audit trail records the significant actions in a system: who did what, when, and from where, each entry carrying a timestamp, a user identity, a source address, the resource touched, and the action taken.

What makes it compliance-grade rather than just logs is immutability: the record must be tamper-proof, so not even an administrator or an attacker who gains access can alter or delete it to cover their tracks.
This is usually achieved with write-once (WORM) storage and retention locks.
Frameworks also require keeping the trail for a defined period, often many months.
